rows.stem: The acid produced in our stomach during digestion and the base used to neutralise the excess acid during indigestion respectively are :
rows.solution:
The stomach produces hydrochloric acid (HCl), which creates the acidic medium needed for digestion. When too much acid is produced (indigestion), a mild base called an antacid is taken to neutralise the excess; milk of magnesia, magnesium hydroxide, is commonly used. Calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) is not used as an antacid, and amino acids and lactic acid are not made by the stomach as its digestive acid.

This is option (A) HCl, \(\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}\).

rows.stem: The part of the flower which attracts insects for pollination is/are :
rows.solution:
The petals are usually brightly coloured and often scented, and it is they that attract insects to the flower for pollination. The sepals are usually green and protect the flower in the bud, and the stigma and style receive the pollen rather than attract the insects.

This is option (C) Petals only.

rows.stem: When a soap is dissolved in water, the soap molecules form structures. What are these structures called ? Draw a labelled diagram of these structures.
rows.solution:
These structures are called micelles.

A soap molecule has a long hydrocarbon tail, which is hydrophobic, and an ionic end, which is hydrophilic. In water the molecules gather in clusters with the tails pointing inwards, away from the water, and the ionic ends on the outside, facing the water. Oily dirt collects in the centre of the cluster.

Diagram: draw an oil droplet at the centre with many soap molecules arranged radially around it, each drawn as a wavy line (the hydrocarbon tail) pointing into the oil droplet and ending in a small circle (the ionic head) on the outside, with \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) ions around the outer surface. Label the oil droplet, the hydrocarbon tails, the ionic ends and the \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) ions.

rows.stem: Explain how equal genetic contribution of male and female parents is ensured in the progeny.
rows.solution: Each parent produces gametes that carry half the number of chromosomes, that is, one copy of each chromosome. During sexual reproduction a male gamete fuses with a female gamete to form a zygote, which restores the original number of chromosomes. So half the chromosomes of the progeny come from the father and half from the mother, which ensures equal genetic contribution of both parents to the progeny.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: What would have been the colour of the sky, if the Earth had no atmosphere ? Give reason to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
The sky would have looked black (dark).

Reason: the blue colour of the sky is due to the scattering of sunlight by the fine particles in the atmosphere. If the Earth had no atmosphere, there would be no particles to scatter light, so no scattered light would reach our eyes from the sky and it would appear dark.

rows.stem: Calculate the resistance of a copper wire of length 1000 m and area of cross-section 2 \(\mathrm{mm^2}\). Resistivity of copper is \(1{\cdot}6 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\) m.
rows.solution:
The resistance of a wire is \(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\).

Here \(\rho = 1{\cdot}6 \times 10^{-8}\,\Omega\) m, \(l = 1000\) m, and \(A = 2\,\mathrm{mm^2} = 2 \times (10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m})^2 = 2 \times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^2}\).

\(R = 1{\cdot}6 \times 10^{-8} \times \dfrac{1000}{2 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{1{\cdot}6 \times 10^{-5}}{2 \times 10^{-6}} = 8\,\Omega\).

The resistance of the wire is \(8{\cdot}0\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
Write chemical equations for the following reactions, giving the conditions for the reaction in each case :

(a) Reaction of ethanol with ethanoic acid

(b) Reaction of an ester with a base (NaOH)

(c) Formation of ethene from ethanol
rows.solution:
(a) Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid when they are warmed in the presence of an acid catalyst (a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid), giving an ester, ethyl ethanoate. This is esterification.

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOCH_2CH_3 + H_2O}\)

(b) An ester heated with an alkali, sodium hydroxide, is converted back to the alcohol and the sodium salt of the carboxylic acid. This is saponification.

\(\mathrm{CH_3COOC_2H_5 + NaOH \rightarrow C_2H_5OH + CH_3COONa}\)

(c) Ethanol heated at 443 K with excess hot concentrated sulphuric acid loses a molecule of water and forms ethene. Concentrated sulphuric acid acts as a dehydrating agent.

\(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH \xrightarrow{\text{hot conc. } H_2SO_4,\ 443\,K} CH_2{=}CH_2 + H_2O}\)

rows.stem:
(a) Name any two pairs of contrasting characters other than height used by Mendel in his experiments.

(b) On crossing a tall and a short pea plant, Mendel obtained \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation in which all pea plants were tall.

(i) Are these plants exactly the same as tall plants of the parent generation ? Write their gene combination.

(ii) Give the percentage of short plants obtained in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation when \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants are self-pollinated.

(iii) In what ratio would you find TT and Tt in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation ?
rows.solution:
(a) Any two:

Round and wrinkled shape of seeds.

Violet and white colour of flowers.

Yellow and green colour of seeds.

(b) (i) No. The \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants look tall like the tall parent, but they are not the same: the tall parent was pure (TT), while the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants carry one gene for tallness and one for shortness. Their gene combination is Tt.

(ii) Self-pollinating the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants, Tt \(\times\) Tt, gives TT : Tt : tt = 1 : 2 : 1. Only tt plants are short, so \(\dfrac{1}{4}\), that is 25%, of the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) plants are short.

(iii) TT : Tt = 1 : 2.

rows.stem: Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable wastes. We generate a lot of non-biodegradable wastes in our daily life. Write any two harmful effects caused by these wastes if not disposed off properly.
rows.solution:
| Biodegradable wastes | Non-biodegradable wastes |
|---|---|
| Wastes that are broken down into simpler substances by biological processes (the action of bacteria and other decomposers). | Wastes that are not broken down into simpler substances by biological processes. |
| Examples: peels of fruits and vegetables, paper, garden waste. | Examples: plastics, polythene bags, glass. |

Harmful effects, any two:

They pollute the soil and water.

Polythene bags and other plastics clog drains.

Cattle die after eating plastic bags thrown out with food waste.

Some non-biodegradable chemicals, such as pesticides, enter the food chain and build up in humans and other animals (biological magnification).

rows.stem:
(i) State laws of reflection of light.

(ii) An object of height \(5{\cdot}0\) cm is placed at 15 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed, so that a focussed image is obtained on it ? Find the height of the image.
rows.solution:
(i) Laws of reflection:

(1) The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.

(2) The incident ray, the normal to the mirror at the point of incidence and the reflected ray all lie in the same plane.

(ii) For the concave mirror, \(u = -15\) cm, \(f = -10\) cm and \(h = 5{\cdot}0\) cm.

By the mirror formula \(\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u}\),

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{-10} - \dfrac{1}{-15} = \dfrac{-3 + 2}{30} = -\dfrac{1}{30}\), so \(v = -30\) cm.

The screen must be placed 30 cm from the mirror, in front of it (on the same side as the object).

Magnification \(m = \dfrac{h'}{h} = -\dfrac{v}{u}\), so

\(h' = -\dfrac{v}{u} \times h = -\dfrac{-30}{-15} \times 5{\cdot}0 = -10\) cm.

The image is 10 cm tall; the minus sign shows it is real and inverted.

rows.stem:
(i) State laws of refraction of light.

(ii) Draw a ray diagram to show refraction of a ray of light through a rectangular glass slab. How is the emergent ray related to incident ray ? Mark lateral displacement in the diagram.
rows.solution:
(i) Laws of refraction:

(1) The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal to the interface of the two transparent media at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.

(2) For light of a given colour and a given pair of media, the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is a constant (Snell's law):

\(\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = \text{constant}\)

(ii) Ray diagram: draw a rectangular glass slab ABCD in air. Draw a ray EO falling obliquely on the upper face AB at O, and the normal NN' at O. On entering the glass the ray bends towards the normal and travels along OO' to the lower face CD. Draw the normal at O'; on leaving the glass the ray bends away from the normal and comes out along O'H. Mark the angle of incidence \(i\) and angle of refraction \(r\) at O, and the angle of emergence \(e\) at O'. Extend the incident ray EO as a dotted line through the slab; the perpendicular distance between this dotted line and the emergent ray O'H is the lateral displacement, and it must be marked on the diagram.

The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, but shifted sideways from it (laterally displaced). The angle of emergence equals the angle of incidence, because the bending at the two parallel faces is equal and opposite.
